items.title: PDL-CUL-25-015, Region of Waterloo Arts Funding Governance Review
notes:
R. Regier, Commissioner of Planning, Development, and Legislative Services, introduced the report and provided an overview of the KPMG findings and related recommendations. He advised that staff are seeking direction from Council on whether to proceed with recruiting a new agency to manage funding arrangements in Waterloo Region on a short- to medium-term basis (three years), or to pursue the formation of an arts council. Julian Kingston, Director of Cultural Services, added that the recommendations stemmed from the KPMG audit as well as ongoing conversations with the arts community.

In response to a question from the Committee regarding the Region’s role in funding non-core services, particularly at a time when resources are stretched, clarification was sought on the rationale for the Region’s involvement in arts-related initiatives. Concerns were also raised about the lack of engagement with area municipal staff and the potential impacts on local arts departments, as the broader arts community was referenced in the report but input from city staff appeared absent. J. Kingston noted that KPMG’s engagement did not include area municipalities. However, a working group has been established at the Regional level to support this work. R. Regier acknowledged the challenge faced in administering the previous arts fund, which prompted the review process. He emphasized that all area municipalities would be included in future discussions regarding long-term options. In the interim, staff are seeking to implement a process that is both effective and timely, to avoid delays in delivering support to artists. In response to a follow up question about internal capacity to carry out this work, J. Kingston described the level of effort and time commitment required, outlining the resource implications.

The Committee discussed the recommendations and it was noted that the creation of an arts council should be considered as a way to remove the political element from supporting the arts and culture community. In response to a question from the Committee regarding the composition of the former Region of Waterloo Arts Fund Board, J. Kingston provided an overview of its structure.

In response to a question from the Committee requesting clarification on the options presented, R. Regier explained that KPMG did not recommend the immediate establishment of an arts council. Rather, the suggestion is to explore this option further, though it remains premature at this stage. He emphasized the importance of engaging all area municipalities in the process and highlighted the need to extend opportunities equitably across the townships and cities.

In response to a question about whether the Region would fund a new organization for three years while also considering the establishment of an arts council, J. Kingston clarified that the two processes would be concurrent. Staff would begin exploring the feasibility of an arts council while moving forward with interim funding arrangements.

Regional Chair K. Redman addressed comments raised by members of the Committee and noted that, having served on the Arts Fund since 2014, she observed that funding was allocated to artists across the Region. She remarked that the establishment of an arts council would be a significant undertaking and noted that continuing with the existing Waterloo Region Community Foundation model in the interim would provide stability for artists who currently rely on that support.

Councillors shared their perspectives on the matter and the recommendation under discussion.

R. Regier noted that the fund is primarily used to support small-scale art installations, and that the Region is not well-positioned to assess the artistic merit of such projects. He emphasized that this type of work is labour-intensive and requires specific arts-related expertise. He stated that any future funding mechanism would be aligned with Council’s overall framework for funding. He further noted that the Waterloo Region Community Foundation has indicated they are unable to take this on in the current year, citing the challenges experienced in administering the fund previously. As a result, they have declined to continue in that role. He explained that if the Region were to administer the fund internally, it would require a significant time commitment and the assembly of an external group of qualified individuals to serve as a jury for the selection process. He concluded that it would be more efficient to proceed with an external organization, following a model similar to that previously used by the Community Foundation.

B. Vrbanovic moved to defer the item. The Committee engaged in discussion regarding the deferral, which was carried.

items.title: Strategic Priority - Resilient and Future Ready Organization
PDL-CAS-25-009, Provincial Offences Court Needs Assessment
notes:
R. Regier introduced the report, noting that the Region of Waterloo is responsible for administering the Provincial Offences Act (POA). He highlighted that the community has been growing significantly, which has led to an increase in offences under the POA. The purpose of the presentation is to provide Council with an understanding of the challenges the POA system is facing as the Region continues to grow.

Julie Medeiros, Supervisor, Provincial Offences Court Administration, delivered a presentation outlining the history of the POA, its responsibilities, POA charge volumes, caseload statistics for 2024, the current situation, and steps that have been taken to date.

Members of the Committee raised questions about the size of current facilities, requesting clarification on square footage and how the spaces are expected to be used. Jennifer Rose, Commissioner, Engineering and Environmental Services, responded to these inquiries, confirming that additional information would be provided. She referenced a space needs report completed in 2024, which assessed both current and future requirements. She advised that staff are proposing to bring a report back to Council in the fall and confirmed that rental options are actively being explored.

The report was received for information.

motions.item_title: COR-CFN-25-010, Q1 2025 Plan and Financial Update
motions.text: That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action with respect to the 2025 first quarter update as set out in report COR-CFN-25-010 dated June 10, 2025: Receive the 2025 First Quarter Update that shows implementation and financial progress towards delivery on the Region’s Annual Business Plan, in support of achieving the vision set out by Council in the Growing with Care 2023-2027 Strategic Plan; and Amend the 2025 Capital Budget and 2026-2034 Capital Forecast as set out in Appendix B.
motions.text_html:
That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action with respect to the 2025 first quarter update as set out in report COR-CFN-25-010 dated June 10, 2025:  

  1. Receive the 2025 First Quarter Update that shows implementation and financial progress towards delivery on the Region’s Annual Business Plan, in support of achieving the vision set out by Council in the Growing with Care 2023-2027 Strategic Plan; and 
  2. Amend the 2025 Capital Budget and 2026-2034 Capital Forecast as set out in Appendix B.

motions.item_title: PDL-CUL-25-015, Region of Waterloo Arts Funding Governance Review
motions.text: That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo approve the process of seeking an independent community partner to manage the Arts Funding program through a three-year contract, in response to the KPMG Arts Fund Review results, and to direct staff to explore the viability and stakeholder support of an Arts Council, as outlined in report PDL-CUL-25-015 dated June 10, 2025.
